source_quote: Clearance and central volume of distribution were 24.0 L/h/70 kg and 43.5 L/h/70 kg for acetaminophen. Ibuprofen clearance and central volume of distribution were 3.79 L/h/70 kg and 10.5 L/h/70 kg. Bioavailability and absorption half-life were 86% and 12 min for acetaminophen and 94% and 27 min for ibuprofen.
source_title: Population pharmacokinetic modelling of acetaminophen and ibuprofen: the influence of body composition, formulation and feeding in healthy adult volunteers
notes: Reported for a 70-kg reference adult; per-kg values derived by dividing by 70 (CL 24.0/70=0.343 L/h/kg, Vd 43.5/70=0.621 L/kg). ka=3.47/h derived from the quoted 12-min absorption half-life (ka=ln2/0.2h). Oral dose range 975-1000 mg from the studied tablet regimens (2x500 mg, 3x325 mg). One-compartment approximation. Simulation only — no dosing advice.

source_quote: Ibuprofen clearance and central volume of distribution were 3.79 L/h/70 kg and 10.5 L/h/70 kg. Bioavailability and absorption half-life were 86% and 12 min for acetaminophen and 94% and 27 min for ibuprofen.
source_title: Population pharmacokinetic modelling of acetaminophen and ibuprofen: the influence of body composition, formulation and feeding in healthy adult volunteers
notes: Reported for a 70-kg reference adult; per-kg values derived by dividing by 70 (CL 3.79/70=0.0541 L/h/kg, central Vd 10.5/70=0.15 L/kg). ka=1.54/h derived from the quoted 27-min absorption half-life (ka=ln2/0.45h). Oral dose range 292-300 mg from the studied tablet/suspension/sachet regimens (3x97.5 mg tablets, 300 mg). One-compartment approximation. Simulation only — no dosing advice.

source_quote: The volume of distribution was 20.2 liters (0.30 liter/kg), and the serum clearance was 13.3 liters/h. The absorption rate constant, kappa a, in the oral study, calculated by the Loo-Riegelman method, was 1.02 h-1, and the absorption half-life was 0.72 h. The AUC after oral administration was 77.4% of the intravenous AUC. On the other hand, recovery from the urine was 43.4% after the oral dose and 57.4% after the intravenous dose, indicating 76.5% bioavailability.
source_title: Absorption and disposition kinetics of amoxicillin in normal human subjects (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1980;17(2):199-202)
notes: Single 500-mg oral and IV dose study in healthy fasted subjects; two-compartment disposition approximated here as one compartment. CL reported as 13.3 L/h absolute; per-kg derived using the study's implied body weight (V 20.2 L / 0.30 L/kg = 67.3 kg): 13.3/67.3=0.198 L/h/kg. Dose range equals the studied single 500-mg dose — no wider range is cited from this source. Simulation only — no dosing advice.

source_quote: Serum concentration of gabapentin was well fitted by a one-compartment model with first-order absorption and lag time. The oral clearance was estimated to be 11.1 L/h. The volume of distribution was characterized as 81.0 L. The absorption rate constant was estimated at 0.860 h-1, and the lag time was predicted at 0.311 h. Oral bioavailability was estimated to be 68.8% at dose of 300 mg, 62.7% at dose of 400 mg, and 47.1% at dose of 800 mg.
source_title: Population pharmacokinetics of gabapentin in healthy Korean subjects with influence of genetic polymorphisms of ABCB1 (J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn 2017;44(6):567-579)
notes: 1-compartment NLME, 173 healthy Korean subjects, doses 300/400/800 mg. ka quoted directly (0.860 h-1). Source values are APPARENT (CL/F, V/F), not true CL/V — CL = F x CL/F, V = F x V/F, shown here: at F(300 mg)=0.688: CL = 0.688 x 11.1 L/h = 7.64 L/h / 70 kg assumed = 0.109 L/h/kg; V = 0.688 x 81.0 L = 55.7 L / 70 kg = 0.796 L/kg. F is dose-dependent (0.471 at 800 mg) — the headline F for this one-compartment model is the 300-mg value; the label's 5-7 h half-life is consistent (ke ~0.137/h). Row dose range = studied single doses. Oral only; first-order absorption is an acceptable approximation. Simulation only.

source_quote: The mean value of the plasma clearance is 10.7 +/- 1.27 L/hr and of the renal plasma clearance, 10.4 +/- 1.14 L/hr. The mean absolute bioavailability for the 25-, 50-, and 100-mg oral doses is 0.52 +/- 0.18, 0.54 +/- 0.12, and 0.58 +/- 0.16, respectively. The mean ( +/- SD) terminal elimination half-life is 6.06 +/- 2.02 hr, the mean volume of the central compartment is 0.173 L/kg. Time to mean maximum plasma concentration (3.0 hr) and the time for half of the bioavailable dose to be absorbed (2.0 hr) do not differ significantly with dose.
source_title: Mason WD, Winer N, Kochak G, Cohen I, Bell R. Kinetics and absolute bioavailability of atenolol. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 1979;25(4):408-415. PMID 428185
notes: Twelve healthy volunteers, 25/50/100 mg oral solution + 50 mg IV; 3-compartment IV model with elimination from the central compartment. ka DERIVED from quoted absorption half-life (time for half of the bioavailable dose to be absorbed = 2.0 h): ka = ln2/2.0 = 0.347/h; the paper itself notes a single first-order absorption may not fully describe biphasic gastric emptying, so ka is a best-fit value. CL = 10.7 L/h (IV) / 70 kg implied = 0.153 L/h/kg. V = 0.173 L/kg is the CENTRAL compartment of a three-compartment IV model, not Vss (subject-level volumes 60-210 L). F = 0.54 (50-mg dose; 0.52/0.54/0.58 across doses). Dose range = studied single oral doses. Simulation only.

source_quote: Table 1. Geometric means (geometric coefficients of variation, %) and ranges for pharmacokinetic parameters of ASA following administration of ASA 250 mg and 500 mg intravenously and ASA 100 mg, 300 mg, and 500 mg orally | F (%) | 100 | 100 | 49.5 | Tmax (hours) | 0.017 | 0.017 | 0.500 | 0.500 | 0.500 | t1/2 (hours) | 0.290 (15.3) | 0.322 (15.1) | 0.395 (52.2) | 0.412 (33.9) | 0.422 (31.3) | CL/f (L/hour) | - | - | 113.6 (44.3) | 106.4 (39.8) | 97.7 (36.1) | CL (L/hour) | 50.2 (18.9) | 48.5 (21.7) | - | - | -
source_title: Pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of acetylsalicylic acid after intravenous and oral administration to healthy volunteers (Clin Pharmacol: Adv Appl. 2014;6:41-9)
notes: ASA/salicylate. CL iv true: 50.2/48.5 L/h (250/500 mg) /70 kg assumed = 0.717-0.693; model row carries 0.693 (500-mg arm). F = 49.5% oral vs iv. CL/f NOT used as CL. Vd NOT reported; ka NOT reported (Tmax is not ka). ASA is a prodrug (salicylate is active) and salicylate elimination is saturable/dose-dependent — one-compartment first-order is only an approximation; do not extrapolate to high anti-inflammatory doses. ke ~1.7/h (oral t1/2 0.39-0.42 h).

source_quote: The oral bioavailability for HCTZ in adults is approximately 60% to 70% with peak concentrations in plasma occurring within 1.5 to 4 hours after oral administration. Plasma half-life is variable, ranging between 5.6 and 14.8 hours, and adult apparent oral clearance (CL/F) is 20.74 L/h (interindividual variability, 34.1%). HCTZ is extensively distributed in tissues with a steady-state volume of distribution in adults of about 275.3 L.
source_title: Pharmacokinetics of Hydrochlorothiazide in Children (J Clin Pharmacol. 2020) — adult values quoted from its introduction; adult paediatric-size section of a population PK paper
notes: ADULT values quoted by a paediatric population-PK paper. F mid-range 0.65. CL/F is APPARENT, not CL: true CL = F x CL/F = 0.65 x 20.74 L/h = 13.48 L/h /70 kg = 0.193 L/h/kg (range 0.178-0.207). Vss 275.3 L /70 kg = 3.93 L/kg. t1/2 5.6-14.8 h -> ke 0.047-0.124/h. ka NOT reported for adults. Dose 25 mg = single dose the source anchors. Labelled clinical range wider but not this source's.

source_quote: The median bioavailability was 39% (25-117%) and the median systemic plasma clearance was 624 ml/min (range of 59-828 ml/min). The corresponding t1/2 for the i.v. dose was 35 min (16-150 min) and 39 min (14-186 min) after oral administration. The drug was rapidly distributed to extravascular sites (mean t1/2 lambda 1 = 3.0 +/- 0.8 min). Mean Vss was 0.23 +/- 0.04 L/kg.
notes: 8 young healthy subjects, single iv 10 mg + single oral 20 mg 14C. F median 0.39 (25-117%). CL median 624 mL/min x 0.06 = 37.44 L/h /70 kg assumed (weight not printed) = 0.535 L/h/kg; Vss quoted per-kg directly (0.23 +/- 0.04). ke ~1.1-1.2/h (t1/2 iv 0.583 h, oral 0.65 h). ka NOT reported (Tmax 10-25 min is not ka). PPI is acid-labile/prodrug: plasma kinetics describe parent drug, not antisecretory effect (duration outlasts t1/2). CYP2C19 variability large.

source_quote: The pharmacokinetics of intravenous furosemide were studied, determining a total body clearance rate of 117.6 +/- 41.3 ml/min and a harmonic mean half-life of 78 min. The mean absolute bioavailability determined by ratio of areas under the plasma-time curves was 64 and 71% for the solution and tablet, respectively.
source_title: Waller ES et al., Disposition and absolute bioavailability of furosemide in healthy males. J Pharm Sci. 1982;71(10):1105-1108. PMID 7143205
notes: 18 healthy adult males. CL iv: 117.6 mL/min x 60 = 7056 mL/h /70 kg implied (weights not printed) = 0.101 L/h/kg. F 0.64 solution / 0.71 tablet. V DERIVED (source gives no V): V = CL/ke = 7.056 L/h / (ln2/78min=0.533/h) = 13.2 L /70 kg = 0.189 L/kg — flagged derived, not quoted. ka NOT REPORTED; source itself notes enterohepatic cycling and absorption-limited (flip-flop) behaviour; an earlier draft's ka cell was rejected as it carried ke, not ka. Dose range not anchored in source (label strengths 20/40/80 not quoted here) — left blank.

source_quote: Naproxen itself is rapidly and completely absorbed from the GI tract with an in vivo bioavailability of 95%. Naproxen has a volume of distribution of 0.16 L/kg. The elimination half-life of NAPRELAN® Tablets and conventional naproxen is approximately 15 hours.
source_title: NAPRELAN (naproxen sodium) Controlled-Release Tablets — FDA Prescribing Information NDA 020353 s028 (2011)
notes: V quoted (0.16 L/kg), F quoted (0.95, in vivo), t1/2 ~15 h quoted. CL DERIVED: ke = ln2/15 h = 0.0462/h; CL = ke x V = 0.0074 L/h/kg. ka NOT REPORTED (controlled-release microparticle formulations dominate the labeled source; not first-order) — earlier version carried ke as ka and was corrected. Saturable protein binding at >500 mg/day and >99% albumin binding at therapeutic levels; one-compartment constants drift with dose. Dose range = Naprelan CR labeled tablet strengths (375/500/750 mg).

source_quote: The absolute bioavailability of a GLUCOPHAGE 500 mg tablet given under fasting conditions is approximately 50% to 60%. [...] The apparent volume of distribution (V/F) of metformin following single oral doses of GLUCOPHAGE 850 mg averaged 654 ± 358 L. [...] approximately 90% of the absorbed drug is eliminated via the renal route within the first 24 hours, with a plasma elimination half-life of approximately 6.2 hours.
source_title: Glucophage (metformin hydrochloride) Tablets — FDA Prescribing Information (2018), NDA 020357s034,021202s018
notes: F midpoint 0.55 (quoted fasting range 50-60%). Source values apparent (V/F): V = F x V/F = 0.55 x 654 L = 360 L /70 kg assumed (weight not stated) = 5.14 L/kg. ke = ln2/6.2 h = 0.112/h. CL/F = ke x V/F = 0.112 x 654 = 73 L/h (1219 mL/min; renal clearance ~600 mL/min quoted — consistent within variability); true CL = F x CL/F = 0.55 x 73 = 40.2 L/h /70 kg = 0.575 L/h/kg. ka NOT REPORTED; Tmax ~2 h is not a rate constant — left blank rather than filled with ke. Renal elimination ~90%; CL falls with renal function — simulation only, not dosing. Dose range = studied doses and labeled max 2550 mg/day.

source_quote: Intravenous administration of amlodipine (single dose, 10 mg) to 12 volunteers gave a mean plasma half-life of 34 h, mean clearance of 7 ml min-1 kg-1 and a mean apparent volume of distribution of 21 l kg-1. Oral administration (single dose, 10 mg) to the same 12 volunteers gave a mean systemic availability of 64% and a mean plasma half-life of 36 h.
source_title: The pharmacokinetics of amlodipine in healthy volunteers after single intravenous and oral doses and after 14 repeated oral doses given once daily (Br J Clin Pharmacol. 1986;22(1):21-25)
notes: CL IV-arm true clearance: 7 mL/min/kg x 0.06 = 0.42 L/h/kg (per kg as quoted, may be treated as F-independent). V 21 L/kg as quoted (CL/F and V/F from the IV arm; used as-is — if read as V/F then true V = 0.64 x 21 = 13.4, noted for the reviewer). F 0.64 (single 10 mg oral). t1/2 34 h IV / 36 h oral / 45 h at steady state. ka NOT REPORTED. Dose range = single studied oral dose 10 mg (labeled adult range not from this source; not used).

source_quote: The clinical dosage range for atorvastatin is 10-80 mg/day, and it is given in the acid form. [...] as oral bioavailability is 14%. The volume of distribution of atorvastatin acid is 381L [...] The total plasma clearance of atorvastatin acid is 625 mL/min and the half-life is about 7 hours.
source_title: Clinical pharmacokinetics of atorvastatin (Clin Pharmacokinet. 2003;42(13):1141-60; PMID 14531725)
notes: CL = 625 mL/min x 0.06 = 37.5 L/h /70 kg = 0.536 L/h/kg. V = 381 L /70 kg = 5.44 L/kg. F 0.14 (parent acid). ke = ln2/7 h = 0.099/h (cross-check CL/V = 37.5/381 = 0.0984). ka NOT REPORTED (absorption essentially complete; first-pass limited). Dose range 10-80 mg/day quoted in the same abstract.

source_quote: After administration of the 10-mg film-coated tablet to fasted adults, the mean peak montelukast plasma concentration (Cmax) is achieved in 3 to 4 hours (Tmax). The mean oral bioavailability is 64%. [...] The steady state volume of distribution of montelukast averages 8 to 11 liters. [...] The plasma clearance of montelukast averages 45 mL/min in healthy adults. [...] In several studies, the mean plasma half-life of montelukast ranged from 2.7 to 5.5 hours in healthy young adults. [...] The dosage for adults and adolescents 15 years of age and older is one 10-mg tablet.
notes: CL = 45 mL/min x 0.06 = 2.7 L/h /70 kg = 0.0386 L/h/kg. V = mid of 8-11 L = 9.5 L /70 kg = 0.136 L/kg. F = 64% (10-mg film-coated, fasted; 5-mg chewable 73%). t1/2 2.7-5.5 h; ke 0.126-0.257/h (mid ~0.17/h; CL/V cross-check 0.284/h matches low end). ka NOT REPORTED (Tmax 3-4 h is not ka). Labeled range 4-5 mg (children) / 10 mg adults — recorded as 4-10 mg; the adult studied single dose is 10 mg. Not dosing advice.

source_quote: Loratadine was rapidly absorbed, reaching Cmax values (4.7, 10.8, and 26.1 ng/mL) at 1.5, 1.0 and 1.2 hours for the 10-, 20-, and 40-mg doses, respectively. The loratadine t1/2 beta ranged from 7.8 to 11.0 hours. Loratadine and descarboethoxyloratadine plasma concentrations and pharmacokinetics were not dose dependent.
source_title: Pharmacokinetics and dose proportionality of loratadine (Hilbert J, J Clin Pharmacol. 1987;27(9):694-8; PMID 2960701)
notes: Only terminal t1/2 reported (7.8-11.0 h). F NOT reported (no IV arm); CL and Vd NOT reported in accessible source; ka NOT derivable (Tmax is not ka). Recorded as blank rather than filled from unverified monograph sites. Dose range = studied single doses. Not simulatable until a full PK source is found.

source_quote: Absorption of orally administered T4 from the gastrointestinal (GI) tract ranges from 40% to 80%. The majority of the levothyroxine dose is absorbed from the jejunum and upper ileum.
source_title: Levothyroxine Sodium Tablets, USP — DailyMed Prescribing Information (accessed 2026-11-12)
notes: No sound one-compartment oral PK: absorption range 40-80% (highly variable, food/malabsorption), enterohepatic recirculation, t1/2 ~6-7 days, 99.96% protein binding, endogenous secretion confounds exogenous PKs, deiodination to T3. Not modellable as single CL/V/F/ka; excluded from import.

source_quote: Volumes of distribution of the different corticosteroids are approximately 0.5 L/kg for hydrocortisone and 1–2 L/kg for the other corticosteroids. Elimination half-lives of corticosteroids are generally short, approximately 4 h for dexamethasone and 2–3 h for budesonide, hydrocortisone, (methyl)prednisolone and prednisone. Bioavailability ranges from 60 to 90% for dexamethasone and from 80 to 100% for hydrocortisone, (methyl)prednisolone and prednisone.
source_title: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Systemic Corticosteroids in Autoimmune and Inflammatory Diseases: A Review of Current Evidence (2024, PMC11450095)
notes: Prodrug: reversible prednisone-prednisolone interconversion dominates disposition (approx 76% of dose recycled) — one-compartment PK of prednisone itself is not sound. Only ranges available (V ~1-2 L/kg, F 80-100%, t1/2 2-3 h); no CL, ka or unbound point estimates. Would need a separate prednisolone-modeled row.

source_quote: Since simvastatin undergoes extensive first-pass extraction in the liver, the availability of simvastatin to the general circulation is low (<5%).
source_title: SIMVASTATIN TABLET, FILM COATED — DailyMed SPL (accessed 2026-11-12)
notes: Inactive lactone prodrug hydrolyzed to active beta-hydroxyacid; <5% reaches circulation as active inhibitor despite ~85% absorption. One-compartment oral model of the administered entity is invalid. F's true interpretation (<5% active moiety, ~85% absorbed) ambiguous for this schema; models should use simvastatin-acid separately sourced.

source_quote: caffeine is absorbed quickly with an absorption rate constant (K01) of approximately 0.33 min -1 in the small intestine. it takes 45 min for the small intestine to absorb almost all of the caffeine and it has a bioavailability of 99% with no noticeable first-pass effects. the mean body clearance of caffeine was reported to be 2.0 +/- 0.8 mL/kg/min in smokers versus 1.5 +/- 0.7 mL/kg/min in non-smokers. The mean volume of distribution of caffeine in infants (0.8 to 0.9 L/kg) is slightly higher than that in adults (0.6 L/kg). One manufacturer recommends that citrated caffeine be administered orally in dosages of 65-325 mg (about 32-162 mg of anhydrous caffeine) 3 times daily.
source_title: Banwo K et al. Caffeine: A Multifunctional Efficacious Molecule with Diverse Health Implications and Emerging Delivery Systems. Int J Mol Sci 2024 (PMC11593559); clearance from Aklillu E et al. Hereditas 2026 (PMC12954933); volume and half-life from the DailyMed caffeine citrate label; dose from the DailyMed caffeine and sodium benzoate label. Per-parameter citations are in data/pk-parameters.csv.
notes: One-compartment, adult, oral. ka 19.8/h is the quoted 0.33 min-1 converted (x60). CL 0.09 L/h/kg is the quoted 1.5 mL/kg/min for non-smokers converted (x0.06). F 0.99 as quoted. V 0.6 L/kg as quoted for adults. Consistency: CL 6.3 L/h and V 42 L give a half-life of 4.6 h against the quoted 5 h. Dose range is the oral citrated-caffeine range from the injection label; there is no FDA-approved oral caffeine product, so no oral label range exists (32-162 mg of anhydrous caffeine is the equivalent). Simulation only.
